newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's ACCC says neutral on media ownership.
newsitem.headline: Australia's ACCC says neutral on media ownership.

text.p: Australian Competition and Conusmer Commission (ACCC) chairman Allan Fels said on Thursday the commission has a neutral stance on the government's policy to Australia's cross-media ownership laws.
"I wish to emphasize the ACCC has no view on what policy options are preferable in relation to cross-media ownership," Fels told a conference on media ownership.
Fels said the ACCC did have views on the need to apply the Trade Practices Act to areas of the economy, which did not apply at present.

"However, with respect to questions about cross-media ownership laws, the issues raised here do not directly involve competition matters and accordingly the ACCC has a neutral approach to policy in this area," Fels said.
Fels said the ACCC mainly thought to outline the kinds of options, which seemed possible to it if there were to be changes in the nature of cross-media ownership laws.
The government has set up a non-public government inquiry into cross media ownership regulation in Australia which is due to report its findings within the next two months.
Under current cross media regulations, media proprietors are not allowed to have large shareholdings in both broadcast and print media in the same market.
The government previously has said it was not predisposed to allowing increased foreign investment in Australia's media.
Foreigners are currently limited to owning 25 percent in Australian newspapers and 15 percent in television companies.

Analysts said if the cross-media ownership laws are relaxed it paves the way for Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd media group to make a bid for newspaper group John Fairfax Holdings Ltd.
